questions.question: Why does the passage say the Qur’an is not poetry?
questions.answer: Because its truths are far too vast and lofty to be reduced to poetic fancy, and its form is not bound by poetic meter.

questions.question: What advantage comes from the Qur’an not being restricted by meter?
questions.answer: Its verses can connect broadly with one another instead of being confined by a fixed poetic structure.

questions.question: How is each verse described in relation to other verses?
questions.answer: Each one is presented as if it can look toward many others and relate to them from its own position.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying many “Qur’ans” are present within the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It means the Qur’an contains many layers and pathways of meaning that speak to different kinds of people and spiritual approaches.

questions.question: What example is given to show that one short chapter can contain many meanings?
questions.answer: The passage points to Surat al-Ikhlas as holding a rich structure of teachings on divine oneness within its brief wording.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare Qur’anic verses to stars?
questions.answer: Because they seem separate at first, yet they are actually linked through a deeper hidden order.

questions.question: What lesson is the reader asked to take from the image of the stars?
questions.answer: That what may look loose or scattered on the surface can still contain a precise inner harmony.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one mark of poetry?
questions.answer: It dresses up weak or ordinary subjects with striking images so they appear more impressive.

questions.question: How are the truths of the Qur’an different from that kind of poetry?
questions.answer: They are already so majestic and radiant that imagination cannot make them greater.

questions.question: What do the cited Qur’anic examples about the sky, night and day, and resurrection show?
questions.answer: They show that the Qur’an speaks about immense realities with power, clarity, and grandeur.

questions.question: What two main reasons are given for why the Qur’an is not classed as poetry?
questions.answer: Its message contains endless exalted truths, and its wording is not constrained by poetic meter even though it is perfectly ordered.

questions.question: How does freedom from meter affect the relationship between verses?
questions.answer: It allows each verse to serve as a point of connection with many others across the text.

questions.question: In the passage, what does it mean for a verse to be like a center?
questions.answer: It means a verse can gather meanings and tie together other verses around it.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the internal structure of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It suggests the Qur’an has a web-like structure full of meaningful links, not a flat sequence of isolated statements.

questions.question: Why is Surat al-Ikhlas mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that even a very short surah can contain many layered teachings within a compact form.

questions.question: How does the star image help explain Qur’anic arrangement?
questions.answer: It shows that apparent separation does not cancel deeper order and interconnectedness.

questions.question: What are readers told to notice in that image?
questions.answer: They are told to recognize a strong hidden order beneath what may first look unarranged.

questions.question: How does the passage define poetry in a critical sense?
questions.answer: It describes poetry as making small or lifeless matters seem grand through decorative imagination.

questions.question: Why would that approach be unfit for the Qur’an according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because the realities the Qur’an speaks about are already greater than anything poetic imagination could add.

questions.question: What do the sample verses about the end of the world and daily cosmic order have in common?
questions.answer: They all express overwhelming realities in a direct and elevated way.

questions.question: What quality of the Qur’an makes poetic fantasy unnecessary, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Its truths are already endlessly radiant and elevated.

questions.question: Although the Qur’an is perfectly arranged, why does the passage still stress that it is not verse?
questions.answer: Because its order does not come from poetic rules but from a broader and more meaningful arrangement.

questions.question: What kind of relationship among verses becomes possible when meter does not limit them?
questions.answer: Many-sided links of meaning can form among verses throughout the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way verses relate to each other almost like living things?
questions.answer: It says each verse is as if it has sight and orientation toward many others.

questions.question: What does the expression about many “Qur’ans” inside the Qur’an imply?
questions.answer: It implies the text offers multiple structured readings and riches of meaning for different seekers.

questions.question: What role does the example of Surat al-Ikhlas play in the argument?
questions.answer: It serves as proof that a brief portion of the Qur’an can hold a deeply layered treasury of doctrine.

questions.question: What tension does the star comparison resolve?
questions.answer: It resolves the tension between seeming looseness on the surface and real order underneath.

questions.question: What should a careful reader learn from that comparison?
questions.answer: A careful reader should learn not to confuse outward appearance with inner reality.

questions.question: In the passage’s critique, how does poetry treat lesser subjects?
questions.answer: It enlarges them through glittering expression and imagined beauty.

questions.question: Why is imagination said to be inadequate before Qur’anic truth?
questions.answer: Because even the highest imagination remains small beside the realities the Qur’an presents.

questions.question: What do the selected verses demonstrate about Qur’anic style?
questions.answer: They demonstrate force, majesty, and the ability to present unseen or vast events vividly without relying on artificial ornament.

questions.question: According to the passage, what prevents the Qur’an from being poetry in the ordinary sense?
questions.answer: Its content is made of immeasurably high truths, and its form is not shaped by poetic meter.

questions.question: Why is not being tied to meter presented as a strength?
questions.answer: Because it gives the verses freedom to connect across the whole text in rich and wide-ranging ways.

questions.question: What picture is used for the relation of one verse to many others?
questions.answer: A verse is pictured almost like a focal point that reaches out to many surrounding verses.

questions.question: What does this suggest about reading the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It suggests that verses should be read with awareness of their broader connections, not as isolated lines.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says the Qur’an offers different “Qur’ans” to different paths?
questions.answer: It means different readers and disciplines can discover coherent bodies of meaning within the same revelation.

questions.question: How does the mention of Surat al-Ikhlas support that point?
questions.answer: It shows that a single short chapter can unfold into many interrelated teachings about God’s oneness.

questions.question: Why are the stars a fitting comparison for the verses?
questions.answer: They can appear scattered while still belonging to a subtle and ordered pattern.

questions.question: What central lesson follows from the star comparison?
questions.answer: True order is not always obvious at first glance.

questions.question: What negative feature of poetry is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: Poetry is said to make weak subjects seem important through decoration and exaggeration.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an stand above that method?
questions.answer: Its subjects are themselves so great that embellishment would only fall short of them.

questions.question: What first explanation is given for the Qur’an’s freedom from poetry?
questions.answer: It contains limitless truths of such height and brilliance that poetic invention does not suit it.

questions.question: What second explanation is given for its not being in verse form?
questions.answer: Its miraculous order works better without the fixed constraints of poetic rhythm.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the freedom of each verse?
questions.answer: Each verse can act independently while still linking meaningfully with many others.

questions.question: What kind of unity does this create in the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It creates a flexible but deeply connected unity across the whole revelation.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying each verse can be a brother to others?
questions.answer: It means verses support, complement, and illuminate one another.

questions.question: Why is the idea of many inner “Qur’ans” important?
questions.answer: It highlights the richness of the text and its ability to address different levels of understanding.

questions.question: What does the reference to Surat al-Ikhlas show about Qur’anic brevity?
questions.answer: Brief wording in the Qur’an can carry extensive meaning and structured insight.

questions.question: How does the passage use the sky to explain the Qur’an’s arrangement?
questions.answer: It compares verses to stars whose hidden relationships become clear when one looks beyond the surface.

questions.question: What warning about appearances is built into that comparison?
questions.answer: Something may seem unstructured outwardly while actually possessing remarkable inner order.

questions.question: How is poetry characterized in contrast to revelation?
questions.answer: Poetry is presented as beautifying small matters through imagination, while revelation presents inherently majestic truths.

questions.question: Why are even strong imaginative images called weak beside Qur’anic truth?
questions.answer: Because the realities revealed by the Qur’an surpass what imagination can fully match.

questions.question: What is the function of the examples about the folded heavens, alternating night and day, and the final blast?
questions.answer: They illustrate the power of Qur’anic expression in presenting vast realities directly.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect the Qur’an’s non-poetic nature with the greatness of its truths?
questions.answer: Because poetry depends on imaginative decoration, while the Qur’an speaks realities already beyond such decoration.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s order even though it is not poetry?
questions.answer: Its composition is perfectly arranged and unmatched, but its order is not the order of metered verse.

questions.question: How does lack of metrical restriction shape the function of a verse?
questions.answer: It enables a verse to connect with many others and take part in a wide network of meanings.

questions.question: What image is used to show that one verse can relate to many others at once?
questions.answer: The image of a verse having sight and orientation toward other verses.

questions.question: What educational point is made by saying there are many “Qur’ans” within the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The text can teach different communities of readers through multiple integrated layers of meaning.

questions.question: How does the example from Surat al-Ikhlas strengthen this point?
questions.answer: It shows that compact revelation can unfold into many linked teachings about tawhid.

questions.question: What does the star analogy teach about Qur’anic style?
questions.answer: It teaches that what looks open and unconfined may still be held together by deep order.

questions.question: What are readers urged to recognize in this apparently loose arrangement?
questions.answer: They are urged to see the perfection hidden within what first seems irregular.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does poetry usually try to do with plain subjects?
questions.answer: It tries to make them appealing by clothing them in dazzling images.

questions.question: Why is that method unnecessary for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Because the Qur’an’s subject matter is already greater than the brightest imagery.

questions.question: What do the three cited verses together emphasize?
questions.answer: They emphasize divine mastery over the cosmos, time, and resurrection.
